emb:L2038590450.exclusion_reason: dental radiography (periapical radiographs for endodontic treatment), not radiologic imaging

emb:L2038590454.model_family: Supervised machine learning classifiers (MLPClassifier, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, CatBoost, and other models; 15 total)
emb:L2038590454.patient_population: 260 TMJs from 130 adolescent patients aged 12-18 years undergoing MRI for suspected TMJ disc displacement
emb:L2038590454.model_description: Morphological measurements (condylar shape, anteroposterior and mediolateral diameters, condylar ratio) and signal-intensity ratios of the lateral pterygoid muscle were extracted from MRI of the temporomandibular joint. Fifteen supervised machine learning models were trained on these features, with patient-level data splitting to avoid leakage, to classify disc status as normal or displaced. The best model (MLPClassifier) is intended as a decision-support tool for diagnosing TMJ disc displacement in adolescents.
emb:L2038590454.headline_result: MLPClassifier achieved the highest ROC-AUC (0.797), followed by Random Forest (0.777) and HistGradientBoosting (0.773); CatBoost had the highest recall (0.839)

emb:L2043451324.model_family: Radiomics with LASSO feature selection, combined with MRI findings (Rad-score based classification model)
emb:L2043451324.clinical_problem: differentiating medulloblastoma from ependymoma in children
emb:L2043451324.patient_population: children with posterior fossa brain tumors: 113 medulloblastoma and 31 ependymoma patients
emb:L2043451324.model_description: Radiomic features were extracted from ADC, T2-weighted and DCE-T1-weighted MRI sequences of children with posterior fossa tumors. LASSO regression selected features to build a radiomics score, which was combined with radiologist MRI findings into a nomogram to distinguish medulloblastoma from ependymoma. Diagnostic performance was compared against radiologists using the DeLong test.
emb:L2043451324.headline_result: Combined sequence radiomics model AUC 0.981 (primary cohort) and 0.939 (validation cohort), outperforming radiologists and single-sequence models

emb:L2047961154.model_family: Machine learning (tabular models combining structured ultrasound descriptors with clinical/lab features)
emb:L2047961154.clinical_problem: appendicitis diagnosis and severity stratification on pediatric ultrasound
emb:L2047961154.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing ultrasound evaluation for suspected acute appendicitis, across 11 included studies (40-780 patients each)
emb:L2047961154.model_description: Systematic review (PRISMA 2020, PROBAST-AI) of 11 studies applying machine learning to pediatric ultrasound for appendicitis diagnosis and severity stratification, most combining structured ultrasound descriptors with clinical and laboratory features. Reviews internal and the one available cross-site external validation study.
emb:L2047961154.headline_result: Internal diagnostic AUROC up to 0.993 (range 0.91-0.96 across tabular models); one external validation study showed diagnostic AUROC decreasing from 0.96 internally to 0.85 externally

emb:L2048017597.exclusion_reason: placental MRI segmentation; imaging subject is the maternal placenta, not a fetal or pediatric patient

emb:L2048090710.exclusion_reason: broad review of federated learning in adult obstetrics/gynaecology, not focused on pediatric radiology imaging

emb:L2048285245.exclusion_reason: adult coronary heart disease model using the Framingham dataset, not imaging-based and not pediatric

emb:L2048747602.model_family: Radiomics with mRMR/LASSO feature selection and machine learning (XGBoost best of 8 models compared)
emb:L2048747602.clinical_problem: screening for growth hormone deficiency in children with short stature using bone age radiographs
emb:L2048747602.patient_population: 271 children with short stature (June 2016-November 2019), grouped as growth hormone deficiency or idiopathic short stature
emb:L2048747602.model_description: The distal radius was manually segmented on left-hand bone age radiographs and 1,562 radiomic features were extracted. After feature filtering and dimensionality reduction, 18 features formed a radiomics signature. Eight machine learning models were trained to classify children as growth hormone deficient versus idiopathic short stature, intended as a non-invasive screening tool.
emb:L2048747602.headline_result: XGBoost model AUC 0.896 (95% CI 0.886-0.979), accuracy 81.5%, sensitivity 71.4%, specificity 92.3% in the validation set, outperforming SVM (AUC 0.841) and LGBM (AUC 0.857)

emb:L2048848637.exclusion_reason: scoping review of robotic neurosurgical biopsy technique in mixed adult/pediatric populations; not focused on imaging AI (AI mentioned only as a future direction)

emb:L2045165920.model_family: Graph neural network combined with Mamba state-space model (Mixing MLP Mamba encoder, Pixel-level Structure Prediction GNN, Maximal Perceptual Feature Fusion Mamba decoder)
emb:L2045165920.clinical_problem: automated fetal head circumference measurement for growth monitoring and anomaly screening
emb:L2045165920.patient_population: fetal head measured on prenatal ultrasound (public HC18 and FH-PS-AOP datasets)
emb:L2045165920.model_description: An ultrasound image of the fetal head is processed by a Mamba-based encoder and a graph neural network module to predict a contour of the head, which is used to compute head circumference. The model is designed to be more robust than prior automated methods to blurred boundaries and acoustic shadow artifacts common in low-quality ultrasound images.
emb:L2045165920.headline_result: On the HC18 dataset: Dice similarity coefficient 98.91±0.76%, difference 0.06±1.18mm, absolute difference 1.05±1.21mm, Hausdorff distance 1.16±0.69mm, exceeding prior state-of-the-art methods; generalization confirmed on the separate FH-PS-AOP dataset

emb:L2038537098.exclusion_reason: uses a simulated/artificial multimodal dataset, not real patient imaging

emb:L2038537102.exclusion_reason: uses a simulated adolescent cohort, not real imaging data, and is a general chronic-disease-burden analytics framework rather than a radiology diagnostic model

emb:L2038476057.clinical_problem: early prediction of selective fetal growth restriction in monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancies
emb:L2038476057.patient_population: 144 monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twin pregnancies (January 2015-December 2024), 44 (30.56%) developed selective fetal growth restriction
emb:L2038476057.model_description: First-trimester ultrasound measurements of crown-rump length discordance between twins and placental abnormal cord insertion were used as predictors in 8 supervised machine learning models, trained on 70% and validated on an independent 30% of MCDA twin pregnancies, to predict which pregnancies will develop selective fetal growth restriction.
emb:L2038476057.headline_result: In the validation set, crown-rump length discordance AUC 0.687 (95% CI 0.4849-0.8881); placental abnormal cord insertion showed limited discrimination; overall discrimination was moderate

emb:L2043418763.exclusion_reason: broad review of preterm-birth prediction models spanning clinical, biomarker and ultrasound approaches; not focused on radiology imaging AI

emb:L2046150576.exclusion_reason: broad review of AI across pediatric care generally (triage, monitoring, NEC, ROP screening), not focused on radiology imaging

emb:L2046532278.clinical_problem: overview of AI applications across pediatric radiology, for pediatric clinicians
emb:L2046532278.model_description: Narrative review/primer aimed at pediatric clinicians surveying deep learning applications in pediatric imaging: chest radiograph models for pneumonia, tuberculosis and malpositioned tube detection; automated bone age assessment; neuroimaging tools for faster acquisition, lower contrast dose and critical-finding triage; cardiovascular AI for congenital heart disease detection and function assessment; and oncologic tumor characterization and segmentation. Discusses barriers including scarce pediatric datasets and limited prospective validation.

emb:L2048549375.exclusion_reason: ophthalmic surgical review (posterior scleral reinforcement for myopia); AI mentioned only as a brief future direction

emb:L2048693442.model_family: CNN architectures (six compared, including Xception and InceptionV3) with pixel normalization, augmentation and ensembling
emb:L2048693442.clinical_problem: pneumonia detection on pediatric chest X-ray
emb:L2048693442.model_description: Six CNN architectures were systematically evaluated on a public pediatric chest X-ray dataset, varying pixel normalization, data augmentation strategy for class imbalance, and feature-level versus decision-level ensembling. Performance was assessed on overall accuracy and clinically relevant false-negative rate rather than accuracy alone.
emb:L2048693442.headline_result: Xception and InceptionV3 achieved the best overall performance among six architectures; decision-level ensembles gave more stable but only modest improvements over single models

emb:L2048749128.model_family: 2.5D deep learning (ImageNet-initialized ResNet-18 on stacked axial/coronal/sagittal reconstructions)
emb:L2048749128.clinical_problem: triage/second-reader support for pediatric craniofacial fracture detection on CT
emb:L2048749128.patient_population: 209 fully anonymized pediatric craniofacial CT examinations from 209 unique patients (103 fracture-positive, 106 fracture-negative), from three centers
emb:L2048749128.model_description: One central axial, one coronal, and one sagittal CT reconstruction per pediatric craniofacial exam were stacked as a three-channel input to a ResNet-18 classifier, as a computationally lighter alternative to full 3D processing, to flag fractures for a second-reader or triage workflow. Explicitly described as a research prototype, not established as clinically effective or robust across sites.
emb:L2048749128.release_evidence: "The proposed workflow is a research prototype for studying second-reader or triage support...The present experiment does not establish cross-institutional robustness or clinical effectiveness."
emb:L2048749128.dataset_size: 209 pediatric craniofacial CT examinations from 209 unique patients
emb:L2048749128.headline_result: AUROC 0.934 (95% CI 0.862-0.989) on development-validation subset; repeated 5-fold cross-validation mean AUROC 0.899 (SD 0.033); leave-one-center-out AUROC ranged 0.604-0.793, showing performance was not uniformly transportable across institutions
emb:L2048749128.study_design: retrospective multi-center diagnostic accuracy study with cross-validation and leave-one-center-out testing

emb:L2038488365.model_family: Self-supervised vision foundation model (DINOv3-based) with Gram-anchoring domain adaptation, multi-scale feature aggregation and a lightweight Primus decoder
emb:L2038488365.clinical_problem: multi-organ segmentation on pediatric abdominal CT, addressing scarce pediatric annotation and poor generalization of adult-trained models
emb:L2038488365.patient_population: pediatric abdominal CT (867 cases used for pretraining; evaluated on the public Pediatric-CT-SEG dataset, 359 cases)
emb:L2038488365.model_description: A general radiological visual representation was pretrained on a large adult CT dataset, then adapted to unlabeled pediatric CT using a frozen adult model as a structural teacher (Gram-anchoring) to align local anatomical topology. A multi-scale feature aggregation strategy and lightweight decoder were added for downstream multi-organ segmentation, evaluated on a public pediatric abdominal CT dataset and compared against nnU-Net.
emb:L2038488365.dataset_size: 867 abdominal CT cases (367,588 slices) for pretraining; 359 cases (Pediatric-CT-SEG) for evaluation
emb:L2038488365.headline_result: Mean Dice similarity coefficient 71.38±1.08% and mean IoU 63.73±1.01% on Pediatric-CT-SEG, improvements of 3.22% and 3.59% over baseline nnU-Net (P<0.05), with larger gains for small organs (duodenum +5.78%, pancreas +4.69%)
emb:L2038488365.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

emb:L2047930028.model_name: GAUGE (GARBH-Ini Ultrasound image-based Gestational age Estimator)
emb:L2047930028.model_family: Multi-task deep learning model with an image-based conformal prediction framework for out-of-distribution rejection
emb:L2047930028.clinical_problem: gestational age estimation and detection of fetal growth restriction / small-for-gestational-age fetuses in late pregnancy
emb:L2047930028.patient_population: 6,579 participants from the GARBH-Ini and WINGS prospective cohorts in North India (development); 1,577 internal test participants; 311 external test participants from a separate ultrasound lab
emb:L2047930028.model_description: A multi-task deep learning model segments the fetal head in an ultrasound image and estimates gestational age directly from image features, rather than relying on standard fetal-size biometry formulas. A conformal-prediction step rejects out-of-distribution images before inference. It was trained on two prospective Indian cohorts and tested on an internal held-out set and an independent external site using a different ultrasound machine.
emb:L2047930028.dataset_size: 46,926 head ultrasound images from 6,579 participants (development); 1,577 participants internal test set; 311 participants external test set
emb:L2047930028.headline_result: Mean absolute error 3.5 days on internal test set (37.2% lower than Hadlock, 25.4% lower than INTERGROWTH-21st formulas); external test MAE 5.89 days; detected 77.6%, 88.7% and 89.7% of fetal growth restriction cases at 26-28, 30-32 and ≥35 weeks respectively, versus 48.6% (Hadlock) and 64.1% (INTERGROWTH-21st) at ≥35 weeks
emb:L2047930028.study_design: prospective multi-cohort development and external validation study

emb:L2048269923.model_name: ASTAR (Automated induction of STAndardized radiology Reporting templates)
emb:L2048269923.model_family: LLM-based framework for automated radiology report template induction
emb:L2048269923.clinical_problem: standardizing radiology reporting templates for fetal brain MRI
emb:L2048269923.patient_population: 4,215 fetal brain MRI reports from multiple centers
emb:L2048269923.model_description: ASTAR is a large language model framework that automatically induces a standardized structured-reporting template directly from a large corpus of free-text fetal brain MRI reports, replacing the manual, expert-consensus process of template construction. It was compared against two expert-curated templates on template coverage, information fidelity, diagnostic fidelity and expert-rated usability.
emb:L2048269923.dataset_size: 4,215 fetal brain MRI reports from multiple centers
emb:L2048269923.headline_result: ASTAR-induced template surpassed two expert-curated templates across template coverage, information fidelity, diagnostic fidelity, and expert-rated usability, reducing template development from weeks of committee deliberation to hours of automated processing
emb:L2048269923.study_design: retrospective multi-center technical development and evaluation study

emb:L2038503510.exclusion_reason: otoscopy-based screening technology, not a radiologic imaging modality

emb:L2044592756.model_family: Vision-language foundation model (Multi-view informed Multiple Instance Learning module and Multi-Level Vision-Language Alignment module), with an LLM-driven report standardization pipeline
emb:L2044592756.clinical_problem: interpretation of fetal cardiac ultrasound for prenatal screening of congenital heart defects
emb:L2044592756.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal cardiac ultrasound screening (5,495 real-world fetal cardiac ultrasound records)
emb:L2044592756.model_description: An LLM-driven pipeline standardizes free-text fetal cardiac ultrasound reports and multi-view images into structured training data without large-scale manual annotation. A cross-modal foundation model (FCUFormer) is then pretrained on this data, learning cross-view anatomical dependencies and fine-grained alignment between image regions and clinical text, to interpret fetal cardiac ultrasound and flag abnormalities.
emb:L2044592756.headline_result: Average accuracy of 87.37% in diagnosis of various fetal ultrasound abnormalities on standardized downstream benchmarks
emb:L2044592756.study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study

emb:L2047456232.exclusion_reason: peripheral blood smear microscopy for leukemia diagnosis, not radiologic imaging

emb:L2047748663.model_family: ResNet-18 CNN with geometric shape normalization (landmark detection, Procrustes analysis, piecewise affine warping) and Grad-CAM interpretability
emb:L2047748663.clinical_problem: pneumonia and COVID-19 classification on chest X-ray
emb:L2047748663.patient_population: COVID-19 Radiography Database and a balanced adult-pediatric mixed dataset including pediatric cases from the Kermany dataset
emb:L2047748663.model_description: A ResNet-18 landmark detector locates 15 points defining the lung contour on a chest X-ray, which are used to geometrically normalize (warp) the lung region to a standard shape and remove positioning/scale variation. A second ResNet-18 classifier then labels the normalized image as COVID-19, viral pneumonia, or normal. Grad-CAM and a cropping experiment were used to check whether classification relied on true lung pathology versus acquisition artifacts.
emb:L2047748663.headline_result: 98.60±0.26% accuracy and 98.00% F1-Macro on the COVID-19 Radiography Database (5-fold cross-validation); geometrically normalized images outperformed non-aligned artifact-masked images, 94.67% vs 94.17%, on the balanced adult-pediatric mixed dataset
emb:L2047748663.study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study

emb:L2047799757.model_family: Two separately trained ResNet-50 CNN classifiers
emb:L2047799757.clinical_problem: fracture detection generalizability between pediatric and adult radiographs
emb:L2047799757.patient_population: pediatric wrist radiographs (GRAZPEDWRI-DX, n=20,327) and a mixed-age multi-region radiograph dataset (FracAtlas, n=4,083)
emb:L2047799757.model_description: Two ResNet-50 fracture classifiers were trained separately, one on a pediatric wrist radiograph dataset and one on a mixed-age multi-region radiograph dataset, then each was tested on the other (opposing) population's data. Grad-CAM was used to visualize what each model relied on.
emb:L2047799757.headline_result: Both models achieved acceptable internal test accuracy (82.2% and 83.7%), but cross-testing on the opposing population caused specificity to collapse to 0% in both directions while sensitivity was artificially inflated to 100%; the FracAtlas-trained model misread normal pediatric growth plates as fractures
emb:L2047799757.study_design: retrospective cross-dataset diagnostic accuracy and generalizability study

emb:L2046878703.model_family: Multivariable logistic regression combining an automated AI-derived chest radiograph consolidation score with clinical and laboratory markers
emb:L2046878703.clinical_problem: predicting macrolide resistance in pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia at hospital admission
emb:L2046878703.patient_population: hospitalized children with PCR-confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: 503 in the development cohort, 138 in an independent external validation cohort
emb:L2046878703.model_description: An AI algorithm automatically quantifies a consolidation score from admission chest radiographs in children with confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia. This score is combined with routine clinical markers, laboratory findings and PCR cycle threshold values in a logistic regression nomogram to predict macrolide-resistant disease at admission, to guide earlier escalation to second-line therapy.
emb:L2046878703.headline_result: Adding the AI consolidation score to the clinical model improved internal AUC from 0.819 (95% CI 0.762-0.876) to 0.860 (95% CI 0.812-0.909; P=0.004); external validation AUC 0.726 (95% CI 0.588-0.863)
emb:L2046878703.study_design: multi-institutional retrospective diagnostic study with external validation

emb:L2047402298.exclusion_reason: study protocol for a future prospective cohort (not yet reporting results); multimodal risk-prediction models are planned using ultrasound alongside many other biomarkers, not a radiology-imaging-AI evaluation

emb:L2047401308.exclusion_reason: ECG-based screening model, not diagnostic imaging

emb:L2047768919.model_family: Deep-learning repeated-measures segmentation approach for harmonized multisite MRI
emb:L2047768919.body_region: brain (subcortical structures: amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus)
emb:L2047768919.clinical_problem: characterizing subcortical brain development in infants with Down syndrome
emb:L2047768919.patient_population: 44 infants with Down syndrome and 39 control infants without Down syndrome, imaged at 6 and 12 months in a multisite cohort
emb:L2047768919.model_description: High-resolution T1- and T2-weighted MRI acquired during natural sleep in infants was harmonized across sites and passed through a deep-learning, repeated-measures segmentation approach to derive total intracranial volume and bilateral subcortical structure volumes. Hierarchical linear modeling was then used to compare longitudinal brain growth between infants with and without Down syndrome.
emb:L2047768919.dataset_size: 44 infants with Down syndrome and 39 control infants
emb:L2047768919.headline_result: Intracranial volume in infants with Down syndrome was 12.6% lower at 6 months and 16.3% lower at 12 months than controls (p<.001); subcortical structure volumes were 6.9-13.1% lower (p≤.003), with slower growth from 6 to 12 months except in the amygdala and putamen

emb:L2046707908.model_family: Multimodal deep learning framework integrating chest X-ray images, ECG signals, and structured clinical/lab features, with echocardiographic ejection fraction as a physiological supervision anchor
emb:L2046707908.clinical_problem: diagnosis and severity grading of pediatric myocarditis
emb:L2046707908.patient_population: two-center inpatient cohort: 5,147 cases (700 myocarditis, 4,447 non-myocarditis) for internal training/validation, plus 529 cases (197 myocarditis, 332 non-myocarditis) from a separate hospital for external validation
emb:L2046707908.model_description: EF-ConsNET fuses chest X-ray images, ECG signals, and structured laboratory/demographic data to detect pediatric myocarditis and grade its severity (mild vs severe), using echocardiographic ejection fraction during training as a physiological anchor to keep the multimodal representation clinically consistent and to make the model's image attention focus on cardiopulmonary regions. It was designed to remain robust when some input modalities are missing.
emb:L2046707908.dataset_size: 5,147 cases internal (700 myocarditis); 529 cases external (197 myocarditis)
emb:L2046707908.headline_result: Internal AUROC 0.926 (myocarditis detection) and 0.911 (severity grading); external validation AUROC 0.812 (detection) and 0.765 (severity grading); performance remained above 0.899 AUROC with up to 20% simulated single-modality missingness
emb:L2046707908.study_design: retrospective two-center diagnostic study with external validation

emb:L2043644856.model_family: Hybrid deep learning model combining a ResNet-50-based DeepLabV3 network with a UNet3+ architecture (transfer learning)
emb:L2043644856.clinical_problem: automated fetal head circumference measurement for monitoring fetal development
emb:L2043644856.patient_population: fetal head ultrasound images (public HC18 dataset)
emb:L2043644856.model_description: A hybrid DeepLabV3-UNet3+ deep learning model, assisted by transfer learning, segments the fetal head from an ultrasound image; an ellipse is then fitted to the segmentation to compute head circumference automatically, aiming to replace expert-dependent, inconsistent manual measurement.
emb:L2043644856.headline_result: 97.83% Dice similarity coefficient, 0.67±2.62mm difference, 1.96±1.86mm absolute difference, 1.30±0.79mm Hausdorff distance on the HC18 dataset, achieved without data augmentation and with ~20 minutes training time

emb:L2043684347.model_family: Self-supervised representation-transfer framework (BYOL pretraining) with a multi-scale attention module and a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network classifier
emb:L2043684347.clinical_problem: automated diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip
emb:L2043684347.patient_population: pediatric pelvic X-ray dataset spanning patients aged 6 months to 16 years
emb:L2043684347.model_description: A large set of unlabeled pelvic X-rays is used to pretrain global feature representations with self-supervised (BYOL) learning; these are transferred into a detector and fine-tuned on a small labeled subset, reducing the need for large-scale annotation. An attention module highlights key anatomical structures, patient age and gender are embedded into the image features, and extracted anatomical indices are fed into a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network to classify developmental dysplasia of the hip severity.

emb:L2046544554.model_family: 3D-SFCN-UNet deep learning framework for brain age prediction
emb:L2046544554.clinical_problem: neurodevelopmental alteration and cognitive impairment assessment via brain age gap in beta-thalassaemia major
emb:L2046544554.patient_population: 275 participants from two centers (139 children/adolescents with beta-thalassaemia major, 136 healthy controls), enrolled May 2020-October 2023
emb:L2046544554.model_description: A 3D-SFCN-UNet deep learning model was applied to 3D T1-weighted brain MRI to predict brain age and derive a harmonized, corrected brain age gap (BAG) and voxel-level local BAG maps across two centers. Mediation analyses linked haematological indices and regional brain features to cognitive test scores, to evaluate BAG as an imaging biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk in beta-thalassaemia major.
emb:L2046544554.dataset_size: 275 participants (139 with beta-thalassaemia major, 136 healthy controls)
emb:L2046544554.headline_result: Model achieved brain age prediction MAE 0.74 years (r=0.93) in healthy controls; patients with beta-thalassaemia major had lower corrected brain age gap than controls (-0.645±1.461 vs 0.000±0.954 years; p<0.001), consistent after age-stratification and propensity matching

emb:L2038289538.exclusion_reason: broad review of maternal-fetal medicine biomarkers (genetic, imaging, AI together); not focused specifically on pediatric radiology AI

emb:L2047401181.model_family: AI lung-nodule detection algorithm, previously trained on an adult dataset
emb:L2047401181.clinical_problem: detecting pulmonary metastases (lung nodules) in adolescents with osteosarcoma
emb:L2047401181.patient_population: adolescents with osteosarcoma undergoing chest CT (248 CT scans evaluated)
emb:L2047401181.model_description: An existing AI algorithm for lung nodule detection, originally trained on an adult dataset, was applied retrospectively to chest CT scans of adolescents with osteosarcoma to detect pulmonary nodules ≥4 mm (a target finding for metastasis staging), and its accuracy was compared against the reference diagnosis, quantifying false positives and false negatives.
emb:L2047401181.dataset_size: 248 CT scans of adolescents with osteosarcoma
emb:L2047401181.headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy 0.843 (95% CI 0.794-0.887); false positive rate 2%, false negative rate 13.7%; using the AI algorithm would increase sensitivity from 0.805 to 0.891, an absolute false-negative reduction of 8.6% (relative 44%)

emb:L2047401656.model_family: nnU-Net deep learning segmentation with IBSI-compliant radiomics and L1-penalized logistic regression
emb:L2047401656.clinical_problem: reference distribution of conus medullaris position and radiomic diagnosis of tethered cord syndrome
emb:L2047401656.patient_population: 9,808 pediatric lumbosacral MRI examinations at a single center; 475 preoperative children surgically treated for tethered cord
emb:L2047401656.model_description: Conus medullaris termination levels were extracted from a large archive of pediatric lumbosacral MRI reports to build a normative reference distribution. An nnU-Net deep learning model was separately trained to automatically segment the conus medullaris on axial T2-weighted images, from which IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted and tested (with cross-validated logistic regression) for their ability to distinguish children surgically treated for tethered cord from controls.
emb:L2047401656.headline_result: Conus terminated at L1 in 85.7% and L2 in 14.3% of the reference cohort (n=9,655); low-lying conus (≥L3) in only 0.05%; among 475 children surgically treated for tethered cord, 99.6% had a normally positioned conus; automated segmentation achieved held-out Dice of 0.85; neither conus position nor radiomics distinguished tethered cord from controls
emb:L2047401656.study_design: retrospective single-center large-cohort reference-distribution and nested case-control study

emb:L2047401476.model_family: Fully automated 3D deep learning segmentation framework
emb:L2047401476.clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of neonatal brain white-matter (internal capsule) maturation
emb:L2047401476.patient_population: neonates (term and preterm) imaged with structural T2-weighted MRI at 7T and 3T
emb:L2047401476.model_description: A fully automated 3D deep learning model segments internal capsule subregions and myelin-related signal on structural T2-weighted neonatal MRI, trained on both high-resolution 7T and conventional 3T datasets. Derived volumetric and intensity metrics were modeled against postmenstrual and postnatal age, with normative modeling used to flag individual deviations, particularly in preterm infants.
emb:L2047401476.headline_result: Segmentation accuracy Dice > 0.95 and relative volume difference < 5% across both field strengths; significant postmenstrual-age-related volumetric and intensity changes; normative modeling revealed significant deviations in preterm infants, especially for myelin-related intensity measures
emb:L2047401476.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

emb:L2043200389.model_family: Lightweight attention-augmented CNN (ResNet-18 backbone with CBAM and Efficient Channel Attention modules)
emb:L2043200389.clinical_problem: pneumonia detection on pediatric chest X-ray, for use in low-resource settings with limited radiologist access
emb:L2043200389.patient_population: 5,863 pediatric chest X-ray images from the public Kaggle pneumonia dataset
emb:L2043200389.model_description: AXNet+ECA embeds Convolutional Block Attention Module blocks within each stage of a ResNet-18 backbone and appends an Efficient Channel Attention head for fine-grained calibration, to classify pediatric chest X-rays for pneumonia while remaining lightweight and interpretable. Grad-CAM was used to check whether the model attended to radiologist-annotated abnormal regions.
emb:L2043200389.headline_result: Test accuracy 93.6%, F1-score 93.1%, AUC 0.964, using only 13.1M parameters and 4.7ms/image inference time; Grad-CAM showed 86.7% alignment with radiologist-annotated abnormalities
emb:L2043200389.study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study

emb:L2043313302.model_family: Multimodal deep learning fusion (VGG16/ResNet50 transfer learning for imaging and pathology, SVM/Hough transform for circulating tumor cell classification)
emb:L2043313302.clinical_problem: early diagnosis of pediatric distal femur osteosarcoma
emb:L2043313302.patient_population: pediatric patients with distal femur osteosarcoma, using public imaging and genomic datasets (TCIA, TCGA, GEO)
emb:L2043313302.model_description: MRI, CT, histopathology slides and circulating tumor cell (CTC) data are each processed by modality-specific pipelines (CNN transfer learning for imaging and pathology, flow cytometry and machine learning for CTCs) and fused into a single multimodal deep learning model for early diagnosis of pediatric distal femur osteosarcoma, particularly to aid metastasis assessment when imaging alone is inconclusive.
emb:L2043313302.headline_result: Accuracy 92.5%, sensitivity 88.7%, specificity 94.3%, AUC 0.96 on an independent test set; adding CTC data notably improved performance for metastasis assessment when imaging was inconclusive
emb:L2043313302.study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study

emb:L2044434939.exclusion_reason: maternal pelvic MRI used to predict mode of delivery; imaging subject is the pregnant woman's pelvis, not a fetal or pediatric patient

emb:L2044642542.model_family: Communication-efficient federated learning framework with online ensemble knowledge distillation (dual-branch student network with an attention-convolution module)
emb:L2044642542.body_region: fetal brain (primary); also tested on brain tumor MRI and chest X-ray
emb:L2044642542.clinical_problem: fetal brain ultrasound standard-plane classification under multi-institutional, privacy-preserving conditions
emb:L2044642542.patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound datasets across multiple simulated institutions with non-independent and non-identically distributed (non-IID) data
emb:L2044642542.model_description: FedFB is a federated learning framework in which multiple institutions each train a local teacher model on private fetal brain ultrasound data, then collectively distill their knowledge (via a small shared public dataset of soft labels) into a lightweight shared student classifier, without exchanging raw data or full model parameters. It was designed to remain accurate under heterogeneous (non-IID) data across sites while sharply reducing communication overhead, and was also tested for generalization on brain tumor MRI and chest X-ray datasets.
emb:L2044642542.headline_result: 91.07% accuracy, 91.28% precision, 91.03% recall, 91.15% F1-score under non-IID conditions on fetal brain ultrasound plane classification, while reducing communication overhead by more than 85% compared with traditional federated learning methods
emb:L2044642542.study_design: retrospective multi-institutional technical development and evaluation study
